top_story.headline: A discharge petition on immigration status sits one signature short of 218 as Congress holds pro forma sessions
top_story.dek: Discharge Petition No. 25 stands at 217 of 218 signatures while neither chamber held a vote on Thursday.
paragraphs: Discharge Petition No. 25, sponsored by Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia (H.Res. 1414), would force consideration of H.R. 1589, a bill to authorize the cancellation of removal and adjustment of status of certain aliens. It has 217 of the 218 signatures needed, with one to go. No petition gained signatures, was filed, or reached 218 since 10/20/2026.
Discharge Petition No. 27, sponsored by Rep. Thomas Massie (H.Res. 1430) on H.R. 185, has 216 signatures, two short of 218.

The floor was quiet. The House met at 3 p.m. and adjourned at 3:02 p.m. with no Yea and Nay votes, no recorded votes and no quorum calls. The Senate met in pro forma session for about 30 seconds. Both chambers are scheduled for pro forma sessions again on Monday, October 26.
No new Congressional Record issue has been published since this one (first covered 2026-10-23); the summary below is carried over.

sections.headline: Two-minute House session, 30-second Senate session, and 59 new measures introduced
paragraphs: The Senate met at 9:00:03 a.m. in pro forma session, adjourned at 9:00:33 a.m. and next meets at 5:30 p.m. Monday, October 26. No Senate committee meetings were held. The House met at 3 p.m. and adjourned at 3:02 p.m., with Rep. Lloyd Smucker serving as Speaker pro tempore. There were no recorded votes and no House hearings.

The House received 53 public bills (H.R. 10855-10907), one joint resolution and five simple resolutions, and filed one committee report, on H.R. 1382. Most of the measures are routine. Among the more notable are a bill to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50, a bill to bar waivers on Russian energy imports, a proposed constitutional amendment on a national referendum process, and an elections-interference bill with a long list of Democratic cosponsors. The full list follows.

items: H.R. 1382, sponsored by Rep. Jared Huffman (D-CA-2) — reported by committee: the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure reported it with an amendment (H. Rept. 119-852). It amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act with respect to San Francisco Bay restoration.
H.R. 10855, sponsored by Rep. Gabe Amo (D-RI-1) — establishes an East Coast Bivalve Research Task Force; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10856 (LIHTC Security Act), sponsored by Rep. Jodey Arrington (R-TX-19) — amends the Internal Revenue Code to keep certain alien individuals from occupying low-income units of qualified low-income housing projects; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10857, sponsored by Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-4) — amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and Public Health Service Act to advance next-generation clinical development of novel treatments and cures; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Ways and Means.
H.R. 10858 (CARE for Blood Cancer Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Nanette Barragán (D-CA-44) — establishes the National Blood Cancer Program; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10859 (Biotech Defense Act), sponsored by Rep. Sheri Biggs (R-SC-3) — requires the Secretary of Defense to develop a strategy on threats from the biotechnology capabilities of foreign adversaries; referred to the Committee on Armed Services and, additionally, the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).

H.R. 10860 (Stop Beijing’s Bots Act), sponsored by Biggs — prohibits the Department of Defense from acquiring or using certain robotic systems from the People's Republic of China; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10861 (Blocking Foreign Cellular Modules in Defense Systems Act of 2026), sponsored by Biggs — provides for an audit and mitigation of covered cellular modules in Department of Defense systems and infrastructure; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10862 (Military Suicide Prevention Oversight Act), sponsored by Rep. Gilbert Cisneros (D-CA-31) — directs the Department of Defense Inspector General to review military departments' efforts to prevent suicide deaths, attempts and ideation among service members; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10863 (Vets and Pets Act), sponsored by Rep. J. Correa (D-CA-46) — authorizes a Department of Veterans Affairs pilot program of grants to nonprofits that provide dogs and cats as pets for eligible veterans; referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10864 (San Carlos Irrigation Project Divestiture Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — provides for the divestiture of certain properties of the San Carlos Irrigation Project in Arizona; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10865 (Samier Amer Foster Care Improvement Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-6) — amends part E of title IV of the Social Security Act to require States to follow certain procedures when placing a child removed from their parents' custody; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10866 (Ronald Reagan Peace Through Strength Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-1) — amends the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act to prohibit the Office of Foreign Assets Control from issuing a waiver for importing Russian energy products; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means with additional referrals to the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).

H.R. 10867 (SLOTHS Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Maxwell Frost (D-FL-10) — prohibits the importation of certain species of sloth; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means and, additionally, the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10868 (Protecting Students from Sexually Explicit Materials Act), sponsored by Rep. Clay Fuller (R-GA-14) — amends the General Education Provisions Act to bar federal education funds for sexually explicit instructional materials in elementary and secondary schools, citing Executive Order 14190; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H.R. 10869 (Protect Clean Water Act), sponsored by Rep. Laura Gillen (D-NY-4) — amends the Safe Drinking Water Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to provide emerging contaminants remediation funding; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and, additionally, the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10870 (Military Domestic Violence Survivors Support Act), sponsored by Rep. Maggie Goodlander (D-NH-2) — extends Special Victim's Counsel services to victims of domestic violence; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10871 (Military Family Relocation Support Act), sponsored by Goodlander — requires information on food access and child care for members receiving orders for a permanent change of station; referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10872 (Combatting Auto Robbery at the Source Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — establishes a National Auto Theft Bureau within the Department of Justice; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10873 (AI Cyber Defense Act), sponsored by Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-NC-10) — requires the National Institute of Standards and Technology to carry out certain activities regarding artificial intelligence attacks; referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

H.R. 10874 (Medicare Low Income Subsidy Equality Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Pablo Hernández (D-PR) — makes Medicare part D premium and cost-sharing subsidies available to low-income beneficiaries in Puerto Rico and other U.S. territories; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10875, sponsored by Rep. Pramila Jayapal (D-WA-7) — amends titles II and XVIII of the Social Security Act to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10876, sponsored by Rep. Mike Kelly (R-PA-16) — amends title XVIII of the Social Security Act to ensure appropriate access to mental health care under Medicare; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means and, additionally, the Committee on Energy and Commerce.
H.R. 10877, sponsored by Kelly — establishes a credit against the excise tax on beer for brewers that donate spent grain for local agricultural use; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.
H.R. 10878, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — establishes an independent Truth and Accountability Commission; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
H.R. 10879, sponsored by Khanna — prohibits noncompete agreements for workers whose annual income falls below specified thresholds; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10880, sponsored by Rep. Young Kim (R-CA-40) — establishes a pilot program for a voluntary federal change-of-address notification service run by the Administrator of General Services; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and, additionally, the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10881 (21st Century Vehicle Choice Act), sponsored by Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH-1) — requires a Vehicle Choice Report from the Secretary of Commerce and makes permanent and increases the clean vehicle, previously-owned clean vehicle and alternative fuel refueling property tax credits; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means with additional referrals to the Committees on Energy and Commerce and Natural Resources.

H.R. 10882, sponsored by Rep. Rick Larsen (D-WA-2) — creates a presumption of service-connection for male breast cancer in certain veterans for purposes of disability compensation; referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10883, sponsored by Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY-17) — provides for nonrecognition of gain or loss on like-kind exchanges of certain residential real property; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10884, sponsored by Lawler — adds options on certain federal application forms to let individuals elect to be organ donors; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means with additional referrals to the Committees on Energy and Commerce, Veterans' Affairs, and Foreign Affairs.

H.R. 10885, sponsored by Rep. Susie Lee (D-NV-3) — ensures delivery service providers have partnership agreements with the restaurants for which they deliver; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10886, sponsored by Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC-1) — requires the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to annually publish a list of dual citizens employed by the federal government; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.R. 10887 (Protecting Consumer Access to Generic Drugs Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Seth Magaziner (D-RI-2) — prohibits brand-name drug makers from compensating generic makers, and biological product makers from compensating biosimilar and interchangeable product makers, to delay market entry; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10888, sponsored by Magaziner — directs the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to carry out a National Centers for Coastal Ocean Science program; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H.R. 10889, sponsored by Rep. Brian Mast (R-FL-21) — amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the retail motor fuel credit; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.
H.R. 10890, sponsored by Mast — amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the motor fuel deduction; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10891, sponsored by Rep. Joseph Morelle (D-NY-25) — removes the limitation on deductions for theft losses involving fraud, deceit or misrepresentation, and allows them whether or not the taxpayer itemizes; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10892, sponsored by Rep. Marie Perez (D-WA-3) — requires household appliance makers to label appliances with estimated performance life; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.

H.R. 10893 (Emergency Assistance Privacy Protection Act of 2026), sponsored by Rep. Brittany Pettersen (D-CO-7) — prohibits use of personally identifiable information collected by the Federal Emergency Management Agency for immigration enforcement; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10894 (Disaster Data Protection Act), sponsored by Pettersen — prohibits the Secretary of Homeland Security from obtaining certain personally identifiable information; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10895, sponsored by Rep. Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA-5) — directs the Secretary of Education to establish a Civic Education and Service Learning Grant Program; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and, additionally, the Committee on House Administration.
H.R. 10896, sponsored by Rep. Keith Self (R-TX-3) — terminates the diversity immigrant visa program; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10897, sponsored by Rep. Christopher Smith (R-NJ-4) — enhances passenger and driver safety on transportation network company platforms through digital verification systems and driver verification protocols to prevent fraudulent use of driver accounts and assaults; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure with additional referrals to the Committees on Energy and Commerce and the Budget.

H.R. 10898, sponsored by Rep. Darren Soto (D-FL-9) — directs the President's Pay Agent to establish pay localities for the Orlando and Tampa metropolitan areas; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

H.R. 10899, sponsored by Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI-11) — amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to provide individual and household assistance during a prolonged power outage; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and, additionally, the Committee on Homeland Security.

H.R. 10900, sponsored by Rep. Emilia Sykes (D-OH-13) — requires States and local governments receiving Byrne grant or COPS grant funds to report to the Attorney General on law enforcement use of automated license plate readers; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10901, sponsored by Rep. Norma Torres (D-CA-35) — requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to create a formula grant program for States to streamline assistance to builders of affordable housing; referred to the Committee on Financial Services.
H.R. 10902, sponsored by Rep. Jefferson Van Drew (R-NJ-2) — aims to reduce crime on public transportation; referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10903 (Socorro Vet Center Act), sponsored by Rep. Gabe Vasquez (D-NM-2) — directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to seek a lease to establish a Vet Center in Socorro, New Mexico; referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10904, sponsored by Rep. Eugene Vindman (D-VA-7) — directs the Federal Trade Commission to convene an interagency working group to track and report on market concentration and monopoly activity in certain sectors; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10905, sponsored by Vindman — prohibits individualized pricing, dynamic pricing and pricing based on facial recognition technology at large retail food stores and their online platforms; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10906, sponsored by Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-AR-4) — a bill “to strengthen American wood”; referred to the Committee on Ways and Means with additional referrals to eight other committees (Energy and Commerce; Transportation and Infrastructure; Oversight and Government Reform; Science, Space, and Technology; Agriculture; Financial Services; Armed Services; and Natural Resources).

H.R. 10907, sponsored by Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA-27) — prohibits interference in elections for federal office; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary and, additionally, the Committee on House Administration.
H.J. Res. 220, sponsored by Rep. Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-2) — proposes a constitutional amendment relating to a national referendum process; referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H. Res. 1634, sponsored by Rep. Becca Balint (D-VT) — supports recognizing October 26, 2026, as Intersex Awareness Day; referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and, additionally, the Committee on Education and Workforce.
H. Res. 1635, sponsored by Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI-1) — supports designating October 23, 2026, as “National Marine Sanctuary Day”; referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.

H. Res. 1636 (Constituent Casework Continuity Resolution), sponsored by Rep. Everton Blair (D-GA-13) — establishes a management system for constituent casework files in the House of Representatives; referred to the Committee on House Administration.

H. Res. 1637, sponsored by Rep. Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12) — recognizes the significance of equal pay and the pay disparity between disabled women and nondisabled men; referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.

H. Res. 1638, sponsored by Sykes — honors and commemorates United Baptist Church's 100 years of contributions to Akron and surrounding communities; referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
